title: Kiki / Agent host
description: The Python agent host: jobs, model requests, images, tools and web calls. The agent host sleeps and exports only after each job, so its series are sparse: time series are rolling 1 h counts and totals one increase() over the selected range, never instant values.

panels.title: Jobs by kind and outcome (rolling 1 h)
panels.description: Rolling 1 h: each point counts the hour before it. The agent host exports only after a job, so a shorter window often holds a single sample of a series and increase() returns nothing for it. Answered job requests in the hour before each point: kind reply, topic, image; outcome completed, failed, running (another request holds the job), interrupted (503, retried). Counts are per request, not per job. The agent host sleeps and exports only after each job, so its series are sparse: time series are rolling 1 h counts and totals one increase() over the selected range, never instant values.

panels.title: Jobs (selected range)
panels.description: Job requests by kind and outcome over the selected range.

panels.title: Rejected (selected range)
panels.description: Job requests turned away: busy (503, no slot freed within 0.1 s), conflict (409, a job ID reused with different input). No data: none rejected.

panels.title: Job duration (rolling 1 h)
panels.description: Rolling 1 h: each point counts the hour before it. The agent host exports only after a job, so a shorter window often holds a single sample of a series and increase() returns nothing for it. Time spent running a job, per attempt that ran it, p50 and p95 by kind. AGENT_HOST_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECS defaults to 120 s. The agent host's duration buckets are coarse (0.5, 2.5, 10, 30, 120 s), so quantiles are interpolated within them.

panels.title: Job duration (selected range)
panels.description: Duration quantiles by kind over the selected range. The agent host's duration buckets are coarse (0.5, 2.5, 10, 30, 120 s), so quantiles are interpolated within them.

panels.title: Model requests per run
panels.description: Model requests per finished reply or topic run over the selected range: mean and p95 (buckets 1, 2, 5, 10; a run makes at most 10). Tool-heavy replies make several.

panels.title: LLM calls by purpose (rolling 1 h)
panels.description: Rolling 1 h: each point counts the hour before it. The agent host exports only after a job, so a shorter window often holds a single sample of a series and increase() returns nothing for it. The agent host's model calls in the hour before each point by purpose and result. Cost: see the Cost dashboard.

panels.title: LLM duration (selected range)
panels.description: Model call duration by purpose. A reply run's duration is the whole run, its tools included. The agent host's duration buckets are coarse (0.5, 2.5, 10, 30, 120 s), so quantiles are interpolated within them.

panels.title: Image attempts: model × result (selected range)
panels.description: Image model attempts by result: drawn, safety_blocked (the model's filter), refused (no usable image, other 4xx), failed (5xx, network, timeout).

panels.title: Image attempts (rolling 1 h)
panels.description: Rolling 1 h: each point counts the hour before it. The agent host exports only after a job, so a shorter window often holds a single sample of a series and increase() returns nothing for it. Image attempts in the hour before each point by result.

panels.title: Fallbacks (range)
panels.description: Attempts on OPENROUTER_IMAGE_FALLBACK_MODEL after a safety block, by whether they drew. No data: no fallback attempts (or no fallback model set).

panels.title: Image duration (selected range)
panels.description: Image attempt duration by model. The agent host's duration buckets are coarse (0.5, 2.5, 10, 30, 120 s), so quantiles are interpolated within them.

panels.title: Tool calls: tool × outcome (selected range)
panels.description: Calls through the tool guard by tool and outcome: ok, error, timeout, refused, invalid_arguments, budget_exhausted (turned away by the per-reply budget).

panels.title: Tool calls (rolling 1 h)
panels.description: Rolling 1 h: each point counts the hour before it. The agent host exports only after a job, so a shorter window often holds a single sample of a series and increase() returns nothing for it. Tool calls in the hour before each point by tool.

panels.title: Tool duration (selected range)
panels.description: Tool call duration by tool (budget_exhausted calls never ran, so have none). The agent host's duration buckets are coarse (0.5, 2.5, 10, 30, 120 s), so quantiles are interpolated within them.

panels.title: Web calls (rolling 1 h)
panels.description: Rolling 1 h: each point counts the hour before it. The agent host exports only after a job, so a shorter window often holds a single sample of a series and increase() returns nothing for it. OpenRouter web searches and fetches made during reply runs, in the hour before each point.

panels.title: HTTP requests (selected range)
panels.description: The agent host's own FastAPI server spans: requests and p95 duration by route and status. Before the agent host recorded this histogram in its duration buckets, its buckets ended at 10 s, so older ranges read a p95 of 10 s for any request that took longer.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_route, http_response_status_code) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="kiki/agent"}[$__range] anchored)))
